chapter: Family and the lake excursion boats
title: Father's pool room record collection; family music and religion
summary: Ernie's father ran a pool room with a phonograph and records by Armstrong and Bessie Smith. He loved music and had a good ear, three sisters sing, and Ernie was Catholic but is now Baptist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, you had a lot of record,
dude? I had records that, man. I don't know what they would have been wasted.
But we had all of them.
See, my daddy used to run this El Rico on San Antonio, Clayborne, the pool room, they call it. and he had a graphing over there. And he'd buy nothing with his Jenny Lindner records.
All sorts of good stuff. Oh, yeah.
All these OK records. They had all the OK records by Armstrong and Mammy Smith, Bessie Smith, all the acts of Butterbean and Sousa. He had all those records.

I tried to find those for Tulane, too. And we have quite a few. We have a pretty good collection now. Always looking for more. Speaking of your father, is there anything more you can tell? You didn't tell us much that you said he was musically inclined or something. What, did he sing some or just like music?
Well, he loved it that much. He loved it that much. He was interested in it. In other words, he had a good year for me, too. He could tell you when it was right or wrong. He had a good eye.
Did you have any uncles or anyone else in the family like that that played or even any aunts that might have played piano or sang or something?
No, but I have three sisters that sing pretty nice. They really love to sing. One of them in the choir, you know, the church choir, the youngest man.
What church did you all belong to? Was it Baptist or Catholic? I don't know.
I was Catholic. I'm Baptist now. I'm Baptist now.
